title: Confluence: Layered Comm Weaver for Multi-GPU Prefill/Decode
creator: Hana Kim
description: Design and implement a layered multi-GPU scheduling subsystem ("confluence weaver") that coordinates tensor/pipeline parallel worklets, selects comm and compute kernels adaptively, and maximizes safe NCCL overlap during prefill and decode phases. Goal: reduce 99th-percentile latency for large-model prefill paths by 20–40% on heterogeneous GPU pools while maintaining throughput and avoiding SLO regressions for small/interactive requests.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prefill 99p latency reduced by >=20% on internal benchmark suite (long-range context models, 8+ GPUs heterogeneous).
No regression (>3%) in mean token throughput for decode-heavy workloads compared to baseline runtime-1.20 on the same hardware.
Automated stress tests (10k requests/min across 4 regions) show <1% observed error spike during rolling deploy using canary policy.
New scheduler integrates with existing kernel-hinting API and falls back to current policy when feature flag disabled.
Perf dashboards updated with per-model metrics (kernel choice, comm overlap ratio, blocked-wait-time) and alert thresholds defined.
design_notes: Layered scheduler concept: split responsibilities into (1) locality/placement adviser, (2) kernel selection & hinting layer, (3) comm-weaving runtime that schedules NCCL launches with computation windows.
Use lookahead windows (configurable, default 5 GPU-steps) to predict upcoming KV-cache reuse and group comm launches to enable partial overlap without ordering violations.

Introduce soft-handoff points between pipeline stages: allow a downstream stage to begin precompute for next microbatch while upstream finishes heavy NCCL AllGather, gated by conservative dependency checks.

Kernel selection will use a score composed of: device utilization, expected tensor shapes, quantization profile, and historical latency variance. Score computed in microseconds and cached per-model-version for 1s.
Avoid global synchronization barriers for small batches: prefer opportunistic NCCL launches with completion callbacks to allow immediate decode progress on remaining GPUs.
Attention optimizations: enable chunked key-query packing for long context prefill to reduce peak memory while preserving KV cache alignment across shards.
Fallback strategy: feature behind runtime flag runtime.features.confluence_weaver; nonzero probability sampling into canary to gather metrics before full rollout.
Compatibility: maintain identical token ordering and deterministic seeds for RNG paths when the feature is off; verify equivalence tests for sampled outputs.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike) - 2w: Prototype comm-weaving loop in dev branch; add lightweight kernel scoring stub and lookahead window simulation. (Owner: Miguel)
Phase 2 - 3w: Implement scheduler APIs, integrate kernel-hint cache, add soft-handoff gating primitives to pipeline runtime. Add feature flags and config knobs.
Phase 3 - 2w: Add NCCL overlap orchestration, completion callbacks, and safety checks for inter-stage dependencies. Implement instrumentation hooks.
Phase 4 - 1w: Run extended perf suite on heterogeneous cluster; tune heuristics. Prepare dashboards and alerts.
Phase 5 - 1w: Canary rollout with 5% of traffic; collect metrics and iterate. Full rollout conditional on meeting acceptance criteria.
testing_plan: Unit tests for kernel scoring logic, lookahead window behavior, and gating primitives.
Integration tests with simulated heterogeneous GPUs verifying ordering invariants and no deadlocks.
Perf benchmarks: internal long-context prefill suite (Llama-70B-like, 32k context), medium-context chat suite (8k), and small-chat interactive. Compare to baseline runtime-1.20.
Chaos testing: inject delayed NCCL launches and transient GPU slowdowns to validate scheduler graceful degradation.
E2E regression tests for deterministic output equivalence on canonical prompts with feature off/on.
rollout_plan: Create feature-flagged build and enable in staging cluster. Run smoke and perf suites (48h).
Canary: enable on 5% of requests in one region (us-west-2) for 72 hours, monitor 99p latency, error rate, and throughput. Backout immediately if error rate >0.5% or 99p regresses >10%.
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 60% over 7 days with daily checkpoints. Stop or revert if alerts trigger.
Full roll to runtime-1.22 after two successful rounds of canary and approval from PM/Performance leads.
rollback_plan: Flip runtime.features.confluence_weaver to false (global config) to return to baseline scheduler.
If rollback fails, revert to previous deploy artifact and route traffic to dedicated capacity pools while investigating.
metrics: kernel_select_miss_rate (percent of times hint differs from chosen kernel)
progress_updates: 2025-11-10: Ticket created by Hana. Initial design brainstorm with Performance and Runtime teams. Agreed on lookahead-window approach and soft-handoff gating.

2025-11-13: Spike complete. Prototype shows 18% 99p reduction on homogeneous 8xA100 baseline for 8k prefill using aggressive overlap; prototype needed safety checks for dependency ordering. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1423)

2025-11-15: Implemented kernel scoring cache and simple heuristic combining device util and shape match. Microbenchmarks added to nightly perf suite. (Commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/commit/7c3a9f4)

2025-11-18: Integration test failure on simulated delay where downstream stage started prefetch too early; added conservative gating and fixed deadlock. Updated design doc. (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Confluence+Weaver+Design)
2025-11-20: Canary harness prepared, dashboards added to Console (prefill_weaver.*). Ready for staging run tomorrow. Assigned QA: Priya Desai.
risks: Incorrect dependency gating can cause deadlocks or throughput regressions under tail events.
Over-aggressive overlap may increase GPU memory pressure and trigger OOMs on large-model prefill.
Kernel scoring added overhead could negate benefits for small/interactive requests unless cached effectively.
Complexity in heterogeneous clusters with mixed NVLink/topology may lead to suboptimal NCCL scheduling decisions.
notes: Avoid coupling scheduling heuristics to a single NCCL version; keep an abstraction layer so we can swap comm backends if needed.
Consider later extension: GPU-aware model sharding hints from model-onboarding pipeline so scheduler receives static topology hints at model registration time.
Coordinate with Dedicated infra team before full rollout to customers with reserved pools—some pool configs may require tuning.
